description: Cases for the size-split sub-issue trust rule (admit.mjs splitChildBody, owner Q93 with the Q9 extension): a body counts as the listed human's text only when the lanes App wrote it, its native parent was filed by a listed human, its header names that parent, and either nobody edited it and every line after the header is a line of the parent's trusted text, or a listed human last edited it (a ticked task box is an edit), which makes it that human's text. An edit by any other account leaves it untrusted. Actors are {type, id} with type User or Bot; parent is the child's native parent number or null; size is the triage Size. admit.test.mjs and resolve-pr.test.mjs read this file. child.parent is null or {number, repo}, repo as owner/name and absent for this repository; a parent elsewhere never counts. A case-level app_id overrides the top-level one, and null means the reader has no lanes App id, so nothing counts.

trusted.body:
## Done when

- [ ] Line 3 says nineteen.
- [ ] Line 4 says twenty.
- [ ] Line 5 says twenty-one.

outsider.body:
## Done when

- [ ] Line 3 says nineteen.
- [ ] Line 4 says twenty.
- [ ] Line 5 says twenty-one.
